items.title: INVESTOR ALERT: RGRD Law Announces that Webull Corporation (BULL) Investors with Substantial Losses May Seek to Lead Class Action Lawsuit Before December 7, 2026 Deadline
items.summary: Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd LLP announces a class action lawsuit against Webull Corporation, alleging the company made false statements about its independence from China. The lawsuit claims Webull misrepresented its operations as primarily U.S.-based when in fact 62% of its workforce and core operations are tied to the People's Republic of China. A House Select Committee investigation corroborated these findings, leading to a 19% stock price decline. Investors with substantial losses can seek lead plaintiff status before December 7, 2026.

items.title: Webull (BULL) Faces Securities Class Action Amid House Committee Findings: “Profound Gap” Between Company Statements and Operational Reality – HBSS
items.summary: Webull Corporation faces a federal securities class action lawsuit alleging misrepresentations about its business structure and China operations. A House Select Committee report confirmed that Webull's data practices expose U.S. investors to PRC surveillance risks, its governance is dominated by PRC-linked control, and its subsidiary accepted conditional CCP government funding. The stock fell approximately 19% to $5.89 per share following the committee's findings. The class period runs from April 26, 2025 to October 6, 2026, with a lead plaintiff deadline of December 7, 2026.

items.title: Is Nvidia, at Bargain Levels Right Now, a Buy? Here Are the Bull and Bear Cases.
items.summary: Nvidia's stock is trading at a bargain valuation of 25x forward earnings despite 700% revenue growth over five years and expected 70% growth ahead. The bull case highlights Nvidia's AI chip dominance, new CPU venture for agentic AI, and massive market opportunity. The bear case cites heavy dependence on AI spending (92% of revenue), potential competition, and China market restrictions. The author favors the bull case given strong long-term AI demand and Nvidia's new growth drivers.

items.title: Is Micron a Buy After Its Latest Explosive Earnings Report? Here Are the Bull and Bear Cases.
items.summary: Micron Technology has surged 270% this year driven by strong AI demand for memory and storage, with fiscal Q4 revenue up over 300% to $54 billion and gross margins at 86%. The bull case highlights early-stage AI adoption, strategic customer agreements through 2031, and continued growth potential. The bear case warns of cyclical memory pricing pressures as supply doubles by 2028, potential AI spending slowdowns, and risks of a pullback despite attractive 6x forward earnings valuation.
